title: Pairing near the boundary of a box-shaped trap in the BEC-BCS crossover
authors: Kelly R. Patton, Daniel E. Sheehy
abstract: We study pairing of attractively interacting fermions confined to a box-shaped trap. In contrast to the infinite translationally-invariant case, where the local pairing order is spatially uniform and undergoes the Bose-Einstein Condensate to Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BEC-BCS) crossover as interactions are varied, in this case the local pairing is expected to vary rapidly near the edge of the box. We address this problem in the limit of a semi-infinite superfluid, finding that the nature of the edge pairing depends sensitively on the coupling. The local pairing exhibits Friedel-like oscillations in the weak coupling BCS regime that are suppressed with increasing coupling strength towards the BEC regime.
summary: This paper theoretically examines Cooper pairing in fermionic superfluids confined within a box-shaped trap, focusing on the impact of boundaries during the BEC-BCS crossover. It finds that while weak coupling BCS theory predicts pronounced Friedel oscillations near the edge, these spatial modulations are suppressed as the system approaches the strongly interacting BEC limit.
main_problem: The study investigates how system boundaries affect Cooper pairing and superfluid properties, specifically analyzing the local pairing amplitude near the edge of a box-shaped trap.
main_result: The local pairing exhibits Friedel-like oscillations in the weak coupling BCS regime, but these oscillations are suppressed as the interaction strength increases towards the BEC regime.
method: The analysis uses integral equations derived from the pairing instability condition, solving for eigenfunctions using techniques involving Fourier transforms and renormalization to handle boundary effects.
model_or_system: The system models attractively interacting fermions confined to a box-shaped trap, relevant to both cold fermionic atomic superfluids (SF) and electronic superconductors (SC). The theory addresses the BEC-BCS crossover in this spatially constrained geometry.
key_observables: Local pairing amplitude $\Delta(\mathbf{r})$, Friedel oscillations wavelength ($\sim 1/2k_F$), and the characteristic length scale $\xi$.
important_parameters: Coupling strength (varying from BCS to BEC), temperature relative to $T_c$, and the hard-wall boundary condition at the trap edge.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a semi-infinite geometry with hard-wall boundary conditions at one edge, and it moves beyond simple approximations like LDA due to rapid potential variation near the boundary.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the suppression of Friedel oscillations in $\Delta(x)$ as coupling increases (BCS to BEC), compare calculated eigenvalues to bulk values, and show representative eigenfunctions for different coupling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem and Hamiltonian, deriving the linearized integral equation governing pairing instability at $T_c$, analyzing the resulting eigenfunctions in different coupling limits (BCS vs. BEC), and finally extending the theory to temperatures below $T_c$ using nonlinear Ginzburg-Landau terms.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles non-trivial boundary physics in quantum many-body systems, providing quantitative predictions for how confinement modifies fundamental superfluid properties like pairing symmetry across a major crossover regime (BCS-BEC).
